description: The shape of the whole inventory in one call: the category tree with an item count on every node (each count covers the node's whole subtree), `statusCounts` per condition (available | in_repair | defect | lost | retired), and `assignedToMe`, how many items the connected user holds, and the first few of them in `assignedItems`. It answers "what do we own?", "how many X do we have?" (the count on X's node, no paging through search_items) and "what is broken?". `myPersonId` is the person RECORD behind the connected login, which is what "me" means in search_items and assign_item. Every number is org-wide and counts published items only; the connected user's own unfinished captures are the separate `draftCount`. A categoryId from the tree is the search_items filter for the items behind a count.
name: inventory_overview

assignedItems.description: The first few items the connected user holds (search_items with currentHolderId "me" lists all)

webUrl.description: Link to this item in the web app, for a person to open. Absent when the deployment has no public address configured

assignedToMe.description: How many items the connected user holds. null when no person is linked

categories.description: The category tree, top level first, with a subtree count on every node

children.description: Sub-categories, same shape (absent when there are none)

count.description: Items in this category AND its whole subtree — the same set search_items returns for this categoryId

draftCount.description: The connected user's own unreviewed captures (drafts are personal)

listUrl.description: Link to the full item list in the web app

myPersonId.description: The person record behind the connected user's login account — what "me" resolves to in search_items and assign_item. null when no person is linked

statusCounts.description: Item count per condition, keyed by status: available | in_repair | defect | lost | retired. This answers "what's broken?"

title: Inventory overview
